**BLUF:** Here’s a step‑by‑step guide to set up a promoted eBay listing on the UK site at a 2.5 % fee (or, if you’re using the default 2 % fee for the first £10, add the remaining 0.5 % to the promotion).

1. **Go to eBay UK**  
   • Log in, then click **Sell** → **Post a new listing** (or open an existing listing you want to promote).

2. **Choose the “Promoted listings” option**  
   • In the listing editor, scroll to the bottom and toggle **“Promote this listing”** on.

3. **Set the promotion budget**  
   • You’ll see a prompt: *“Set a budget (Budget %)*.”  
   – Enter **2.5** in the “Budget %” field.  
   – If the UI only allows a minimum of 2 %, type **2.5** and confirm; eBay will automatically apply the extra 0.5 % to the promotion fee.

4. **Adjust the maximum weekly cost** (optional)  
   • Under **Budget %** you can also set a limit for how much you’re willing to spend each week—use this to keep the promotion cost under a certain amount.

5. **Add performance goals** (optional)  
   • You can set a **Performance goal** (e.g., “Buy Now” or “Watchers”) that eBay will target for your promotion. Leave it at “None” if you want a general reach.

6. **Finish the listing**  
   • Complete the rest of the listing details, then click **Post item**.  
   – eBay will show a preview of the promotion bar and the adjusted 2.5 % promotional fee.

7. **Monitor the promotion**  
   • After posting, go to **My eBay → Promotions** to see the performance and cost.  
   – If you notice the cost slipping above your target, adjust the budget % or the weekly cap.

**Quick tips:**  
• 2.5 % is slightly higher than the default 2 % fee for items under £10, so you’ll see that exact threshold reflected in the “Cost of promotion” column.  
• If your item price is above £120, the promo fee is capped at £9.84 (2 % of the price) plus your budget %; make sure the budget matches your budget % limit.

Let me know if you’d like to tweak any part of this or set a different budget.
